terms.name: Viral and Parasitic Diseases of Veterinary Medicine

posts.post_title: How many serotypes of Foot and Mouth Disease…
posts.post_content: How many serotypes of Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD) virus have been identified worldwide?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: 7

Seven serotypes of FMD virus are recognised globally.

Correct Option Explanation

The serotypes are O, A, C, SAT-1, SAT-2, SAT-3 and Asia-1; infection with one serotype does not confer immunity against another.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • 5 understates the number of recognised FMDV serotypes.
  • 6 is one short of the true count of seven serotypes.
  • 8 overstates the number; only seven serotypes are recognised.
Know More
  • In India, only O, A, C and Asia-1 occur.
  • Apthovirus is a positive-sense, single-stranded RNA virus.
  • Subtypes A22, A5 and A10 are common in India.
  • Cattle are most susceptible, followed by pigs.
  • Morbidity can reach 100% with mortality below 2%.

posts.post_title: Which FMD serotypes occur in India?
posts.post_content: Which of the following combinations of Foot and Mouth Disease virus serotypes are known to occur in India?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: O, A, C and Asia-1

Only four major serotypes circulate in India.

Correct Option Explanation

Among these, subtypes A22, A5 and A10 are the most commonly occurring in the country.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • SAT-1 and SAT-2 are African serotypes, not reported in India.
  • SAT-2 and SAT-3 are African territory serotypes, not Indian.
  • SAT-1 and SAT-3 are not among the four serotypes recorded in India.
Know More
  • Seven serotypes exist worldwide: O, A, C, SAT-1, SAT-2, SAT-3, Asia-1.
  • Horse is refractory to FMDV infection.
  • Main transmission route is inhalation/aerosol.
  • Incubation period ranges from 2 days to 3 weeks.

posts.post_title: Cell line highly suitable for FMDV multiplic…
posts.post_content: Which of the following cell lines is highly suitable for the multiplication of Foot and Mouth Disease virus?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: BHK-21

Baby Hamster Kidney-21 (BHK-21) cells are highly suitable for FMDV growth.

Correct Option Explanation

Along with IB-RS-2 cells, BHK-21 supports cytopathic effect within 24–48 hours; the virus is highly cytolytic.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Vero cells (African green monkey kidney) are not cited for FMDV isolation here.
  • MDCK cells are canine kidney cells used mainly for influenza virus isolation.
  • HeLa cells are a human cervical cancer line, not used for FMDV culture here.
Know More
  • Primary bovine tongue epithelium and pig kidney cells are also used.
  • Guinea pigs and suckling mice serve as experimental animals.
  • Some strains grow in 14-day-old embryonated eggs.
  • Route of egg inoculation: chorioallantoic membrane or intravenous.

posts.post_title: Species refractory to FMD virus infection
posts.post_content: Which of the following domestic animal species is refractory to Foot and Mouth Disease virus (FMDV) infection?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Horse

The horse does not develop natural FMDV infection.

Correct Option Explanation

Horses are refractory to FMDV, unlike cloven-hoofed species which are naturally susceptible.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Cattle are the most susceptible species to FMD.
  • Pig is susceptible and ranks after cattle in susceptibility.
  • Goat can be affected, though the disease is comparatively rare in small ruminants.
Know More
  • Man can acquire mild FMD with hand vesicles.
  • Wild species like African buffalo, elephants, deer are susceptible.
  • Abortion in cattle mostly occurs in the second trimester.
  • Calves up to 6 months can die from myocarditis.

posts.post_title: Most commonly used serological test for FMD…
posts.post_content: Which serological test is most commonly used and considered important to identify the serotype of Foot and Mouth Disease virus?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Complement Fixation Test

CFT is the most commonly used test for FMDV typing.

Correct Option Explanation

In CFT, the suspension of the original serum is used as antibody to identify the virus type.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Agar Gel Immunodiffusion (gel diffusion test) is a supplementary, not the primary, test named.
  • Haemagglutination test is not among the FMDV diagnostic tests listed.
  • Rose Bengal Plate Test is used for brucellosis, not FMD.
Know More
  • ELISA and PCR are now standard reference-lab methods.
  • Samples are transported in phosphate buffer saline pH 7.6.
  • Container is disinfected with 4% Na2CO3 or 0.2% citric acid.
  • Virus/serum neutralisation tests detect antibodies in recovered animals.

posts.post_title: Genus of the Rinderpest virus
posts.post_content: The Rinderpest virus belongs to which genus within the family Paramyxoviridae?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Morbillivirus

Rinderpest virus is a Morbillivirus within family Paramyxoviridae.

Correct Option Explanation

It is a negative-strand RNA virus, immunologically related to measles and canine distemper viruses.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Pneumovirus genus includes respiratory syncytial virus, unrelated to rinderpest.
  • Rubulavirus genus includes mumps and parainfluenza viruses, not rinderpest.
  • Henipavirus genus includes Nipah and Hendra viruses, not rinderpest.
Know More
  • Rinderpest is also called cattle plague.
  • Hill Zebu cattle are more susceptible than Plain Zebu in India.
  • Only a single serotype exists, with varying pathotypes.
  • Disease has been eradicated from India.

posts.post_title: Characteristic cytopathic effect of Rinderpe…
posts.post_content: The cytopathic effect produced by Rinderpest virus in susceptible cell cultures is characterised by the formation of which of the following?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Syncytia (multinucleated giant cells)

Rinderpest virus produces large, well-defined multinucleated giant cells called syncytia.

Correct Option Explanation

Infected cultures also show stellate/spindle-shaped cells with anastomosing processes and both intracytoplasmic and intranuclear inclusion bodies.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Intranuclear crystalline arrays alone do not describe the described syncytial CPE.
  • Cell rounding without fusion contradicts the syncytium-forming nature of the virus.
  • Plaque-free degeneration is inconsistent with the giant-cell CPE described.
Know More
  • Virus multiplies in the cytoplasm of host cells like Vero cells.
  • Disease has 4 clinical stages: incubation, prodromal, mucosal, diarrhoeic.
  • Mortality in cattle, sheep, goats and pigs can reach 90%.
  • Incubation period is 2–9 days.

posts.post_title: Preservative that must not be used for Rinde…
posts.post_content: Which of the following preservatives should NOT be used while collecting samples for isolation of Rinderpest virus?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Glycerol

Glycerol should not be used as a preservative for Rinderpest virus samples.

Correct Option Explanation

Glycerol inactivates the labile Rinderpest virus, so blood is instead collected into heparin or EDTA for leukocyte isolation.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Heparin is a suitable anticoagulant for collecting blood to isolate the leukocyte fraction.
  • EDTA (ethylene diamine tetra acetic acid) is likewise a suitable anticoagulant for sample collection.
  • Phosphate buffer saline is a standard transport medium, not the prohibited one here.
Know More
  • Virus is isolated on B95a marmoset lymphoblastoid or Vero cells.
  • Serological tests include AGID, VNT, competitive ELISA.
  • RT-PCR is used for molecular diagnosis.
  • Differentials include haemorrhagic septicaemia and FMD.

posts.post_title: Duration of immunity from goat tissue Rinder…
posts.post_content: The goat tissue vaccine against Rinderpest confers immunity lasting for approximately how long?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: 13 years or lifelong

The goat tissue vaccine gives immunity lasting 13 years or lifelong.

Correct Option Explanation

This contrasts with the Laprinised vaccine, whose immunity lasts only 1–7 years.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • 1–7 years describes the duration of immunity from the Laprinised vaccine, not the goat tissue vaccine.
  • 6 months is far shorter than the actual duration conferred by the goat tissue vaccine.
  • 2–4 weeks does not correspond to any stated Rinderpest vaccine immunity duration.
Know More
  • Kabete 'O' strain attenuated tissue-culture vaccine gives lifelong immunity.
  • Vaccine grown on bovine kidney or Vero cells.
  • Calves vaccinated at 6–12 months of age in endemic areas.
  • Caustic soda and Lysol have high virucidal activity against the virus.

posts.post_title: Normal route of Rinderpest virus infection
posts.post_content: What is the normal route of infection of Rinderpest virus in cattle?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Nasopharyngeal mucosa

The nasopharyngeal mucosa is the normal route of Rinderpest infection.

Correct Option Explanation

The virus is transmitted in aerosols from sick to susceptible animals over close contact, entering via the nasopharynx.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Conjunctival route is not cited as the normal route for Rinderpest.
  • Percutaneous route is not described as a route of natural infection here.
  • Transplacental route is not mentioned as a route of Rinderpest transmission.
Know More
  • Transmission by ingestion of contaminated food/water is rare.
  • Morbidity in susceptible populations can reach 100%.
  • Mortality ranges from 90–100% in acute cases.
  • Disease is enzootic in northern equatorial Africa and the Middle East.

posts.post_title: Genus and family of Bovine Viral Diarrhoea v…
posts.post_content: Bovine Viral Diarrhoea virus (BVDV) belongs to which genus and family?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Pestivirus, Flaviviridae

BVDV is a single-stranded RNA virus of genus Pestivirus, family Flaviviridae.

Correct Option Explanation

It is closely related to classical swine fever virus and Ovine Border disease virus, both also Pestiviruses.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Morbillivirus/Paramyxoviridae describes Rinderpest virus, not BVDV.
  • Aphthovirus/Picornaviridae describes the FMD virus, not BVDV.
  • Orbivirus/Reoviridae describes the Bluetongue virus, not BVDV.
Know More
  • Two genotypes of BVDV co-circulate worldwide.
  • Two biotypes exist: cytopathogenic and non-cytopathogenic.
  • Persistently infected animals are the main source of virus in nature.
  • Quarantine period for newly purchased cattle is 30 days.

posts.post_title: Gestational age at which BVDV infection caus…
posts.post_content: Fetal infection with non-cytopathogenic Bovine Viral Diarrhoea virus before the age of immunocompetence, at around which stage of gestation, leads to lifelong persistent infection?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: 110–120 days

Infection before 110–120 days of gestation leads to lifelong persistence.

Correct Option Explanation

Before immunocompetence develops, the virus is accepted as self, producing lifelong immune tolerance and lack of antibody.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • 30–40 days is earlier than the gestational window specifically cited for persistence.
  • 150–170 days is later than the stated critical window before immunocompetence.
  • The last month of gestation is well after the fetal immune system matures.
Know More
  • Superinfection with cytopathogenic biotype at 6–18 months age can cause MD.
  • Mucosal disease (MD) has high mortality, low morbidity.
  • Mortality in persistently infected cattle exceeds 50% at 6–18 months.
  • Modified live BVD vaccine is unsafe for pregnant cattle.

posts.post_title: Age group most commonly affected by acute po…
posts.post_content: Acute post-natal infection of susceptible non-pregnant cattle with Bovine Viral Diarrhoea virus is most common in animals of which age group?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: 8–24 months

Acute BVD infection is most common in cattle aged 8–24 months.

Correct Option Explanation

Colostral antibody in calves declines by 3–8 months of age, leaving them susceptible thereafter.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • 0–2 months calves are largely protected by colostral antibody.
  • 3–4 years is older than the peak susceptibility window described.
  • Over 6 years is not the age group associated with acute infection here.
Know More
  • Incubation period of acute BVD is 5–7 days.
  • Fever reaches 40–41°C with leucopenia and viraemia.
  • Virus causes transient immunosuppression via reduced interferon.
  • Venereal spread occurs via semen of persistently infected bulls.

posts.post_title: Causative agents of Malignant Catarrhal Fever
posts.post_content: Malignant Catarrhal Fever (MCF) in cattle is caused by which of the following viruses?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Ovine herpesvirus-1 and Alcelaphine herpesvirus-2

MCF is caused by Ovine herpesvirus-1 and Alcelaphine herpesvirus-2, family Herpesviridae.

Correct Option Explanation

Sheep act as the indicator host while wildebeest are the reservoir host that transmit the disease to cattle.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Bovine herpesvirus-1 causes Infectious Bovine Rhinotracheitis, a differential diagnosis, not MCF.
  • BVDV is a Pestivirus causing bovine viral diarrhoea, listed only as a differential for MCF.
  • Bluetongue virus is an Orbivirus of sheep, unrelated to MCF's causative agents.
Know More
  • Wildebeest viraemia can persist up to 3 months.
  • Incubation period of MCF ranges from 2–8 weeks.
  • Disease is almost invariably fatal in cattle.
  • No reliable serological test exists; diagnosis is clinical.

posts.post_title: Reservoir host for Malignant Catarrhal Fever…
posts.post_content: Which of the following serves as the reservoir host for the Malignant Catarrhal Fever virus?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Wildebeest and wild rabbits

Wildebeest and wild rabbits are the reservoir hosts for MCF virus.

Correct Option Explanation

Sheep act only as the sub-clinically infected indicator host through which cattle acquire infection.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Domestic sheep are the indicator host, not the reservoir host, for MCF.
  • Cattle are the susceptible clinically affected species, not a reservoir.
  • Buffalo are also a susceptible species affected by MCF, not the reservoir.
Know More
  • MCF causes keratoconjunctivitis and generalized lymph node enlargement.
  • Head and eye form runs a clinical course of about 9 days.
  • Fever can range from 105–108°F.
  • Cattle should be kept separate from sheep as prevention.

posts.post_title: Causative virus and 'Red nose' synonym of IBR
posts.post_content: Infectious Bovine Rhinotracheitis (IBR), also known as 'Red nose', is caused by which virus?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Bovine herpesvirus-1

IBR is caused by Bovine herpesvirus-1, a DNA virus.

Correct Option Explanation

It belongs to family Herpesviridae, subfamily Alphaherpesvirinae, genus Varicellovirus.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Bovine herpesvirus-4 is a different bovine herpesvirus, not the IBR agent.
  • BVD virus is a Pestivirus causing a distinct disease, not IBR.
  • Parainfluenza-3 virus causes a different bovine respiratory disease, not IBR.
Know More
  • Severe nasal congestion gives the name 'Red nose'.
  • Disease also affects goat, swine, buffaloes.
  • Recorded in Indian states like Uttar Pradesh, Kerala, Gujarat.
  • CPE develops in cell culture within 2–4 days.

posts.post_title: Timing of foetal death in the abortive form…
posts.post_content: In the abortive form of Infectious Bovine Rhinotracheitis, the foetus most typically dies and is expelled at approximately what stage of gestation?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: 4 months

The foetus commonly dies at around 4 months of gestation in IBR abortions.

Correct Option Explanation

Abortion may occur as an 'abortion storm', with the expelled foetus usually found autolysed.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • 1 month is earlier than the described typical timing of foetal death.
  • 7 months is later than the described 4-month timing.
  • Full-term death does not match the described abortive presentation.
Know More
  • IBR also has respiratory, vulvo-vaginal, ocular and encephalomyelitic forms.
  • Encephalomyelitic form causes death within 4 days of neurological signs.
  • MLV vaccine is contraindicated in pregnant cows due to abortigenicity.
  • Calves are vaccinated after 5 months of age.

posts.post_title: Cell line commonly used for IBR virus isolat…
posts.post_content: Which of the following cell lines is commonly used for isolating the Infectious Bovine Rhinotracheitis virus?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Madin-Darby Bovine Kidney (MDBK) cell line

The MDBK cell line, along with secondary lung/kidney cells, is used for IBR virus isolation.

Correct Option Explanation

These bovine-origin cultures allow the virus to produce cytopathic effect within 2–4 days.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • BHK-21 is highlighted for FMD virus isolation, not IBR.
  • Vero cells are cited for Rinderpest virus work, not specifically IBR here.
  • Chicken embryo fibroblasts are typically used for avian viruses, not IBR.
Know More
  • Virus neutralisation test and ELISA are the main serological tests.
  • Droplet infection is the chief mode of transmission.
  • Differential diagnoses include CBPP and pasteurellosis.
  • Killed vaccine doses are given 4 weeks apart.

posts.post_title: IBR form causing pustular balanoposthitis in…
posts.post_content: Which clinical form of Infectious Bovine Rhinotracheitis produces pustular balanoposthitis in bulls?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Vulvo-vaginal form

The vulvo-vaginal form produces pustular balanoposthitis in bulls.

Correct Option Explanation

Semen from affected bulls becomes contaminated, causing problems in natural or artificial breeding.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Respiratory form is marked by dyspnoea and nasal discharge, not genital lesions.
  • Ocular form involves conjunctivitis and corneal opacity, not balanoposthitis.
  • Encephalomyelitic form causes nervous signs like circling and coma, not genital lesions.
Know More
  • Vulvo-vaginal form causes a sharp fall in milk yield.
  • Cows show frequent urination and vulvar swelling.
  • Respiratory form is nicknamed 'Red nose'.
  • Ocular form may show petechial haemorrhages on conjunctiva.

posts.post_title: Time to develop immunity after IBR vaccinati…
posts.post_content: After vaccination against Infectious Bovine Rhinotracheitis, immunity in calves typically develops within how many days?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: 10–14 days

Immunity develops within 10–14 days of IBR vaccination.

Correct Option Explanation

Calves are vaccinated after 5 months of age, with live vaccines inducing both humoral and cell-mediated responses.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • 1–2 days is too short a period for protective immunity to develop.
  • 30–45 days overstates the time needed to develop immunity after vaccination.
  • 60–90 days is far longer than the actual described immunity onset period.
Know More
  • Killed vaccine doses are repeated four weeks apart with annual boosters.
  • MLV vaccine can be given via intramuscular or intranasal route.
  • Seropositive latent carriers should be identified and eliminated from herds.
  • Differential diagnosis includes CBPP and Parainfluenza infection.

posts.post_title: Viral family of Bovine Leukemia Virus
posts.post_content: Bovine Leukemia Virus (BLV), the causative agent of Enzootic Bovine Leukosis, belongs to which viral family?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Retroviridae

BLV belongs to family Retroviridae, and only one antigenic type has been identified.

Correct Option Explanation

The virus produces syncytia in cell culture, used as an assay for virus or antibody detection.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Herpesviridae includes IBR and MCF viruses, not BLV.
  • Flaviviridae includes BVDV, not BLV.
  • Paramyxoviridae includes Rinderpest virus, not BLV.
Know More
  • About 80% of a dairy herd may be infected inapparently.
  • Only ~2% of infected animals develop overt disease.
  • 10–15% of calves born to infected cows are vertically infected.
  • Disease is a B-cell lymphoma mainly of dairy cattle over 2 years.

posts.post_title: Common tests for Bovine Leukemia Virus antib…
posts.post_content: Which of the following serological tests are widely used for antibody detection in Enzootic Bovine Leukosis eradication programmes?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Agar gel immunodiffusion (AGID) and ELISA

AGID and ELISA (serum or milk) are the widely used antibody tests for BLV.

Correct Option Explanation

These tests underpin successful eradication policies by identifying and removing seropositive cattle.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Complement fixation test is emphasised for FMD typing, not BLV serology.
  • Rose Bengal Plate Test is a brucellosis test, unrelated to BLV.
  • Haemagglutination inhibition test is not cited among BLV diagnostic tests.
Know More
  • Proviral DNA can be detected in lymphocytes by PCR.
  • No vaccine is available to prevent bovine leukosis.
  • Non-viral sporadic leukosis forms occur in younger animals.
  • Cattle and buffaloes are the most susceptible hosts.

posts.post_title: Genus of Bovine Ephemeral Fever virus
posts.post_content: Bovine Ephemeral Fever (BEF) virus, also called Three-day sickness, belongs to which genus?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Rhabdovirus

BEF virus belongs to genus Rhabdovirus and is related to human dengue fever virus.

Correct Option Explanation

It causes a benign, arthropod-borne, non-contagious febrile illness in cattle and buffalo.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Pestivirus genus contains BVDV, not the BEF agent.
  • Orbivirus genus contains Bluetongue virus, unrelated to BEF.
  • Morbillivirus genus contains Rinderpest virus, not BEF.
Know More
  • BEF is also called Dragon Boat disease.
  • Cattle aged 6 months to 2 years are more susceptible.
  • Main vectors are Ceratopogonidae (sand flies) and mosquitoes.
  • Morbidity can reach 100% with fatality around 1%.

posts.post_title: Characteristic posture in Bovine Ephemeral F…
posts.post_content: Which characteristic posture, resembling acute laminitis, is seen in cattle affected with Bovine Ephemeral Fever?

_aimcq_options.text: All four feet bunched under the body

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: All four feet bunched under the body

Affected cattle show a posture with all four feet bunched under the body, resembling laminitis.

Correct Option Explanation

This appears alongside severe muscular stiffness on the second day of the biphasic/triphasic fever.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Dog-sitting posture is not the stance described for BEF.
  • Star-gazing posture is associated with other neurological conditions, not BEF.
  • Sawhorse stance is classically linked to tetanus, not BEF.
Know More
  • Some animals show sternal recumbency from hypocalcaemia (milk fever posture).
  • Sample of choice is blood buffy coat and serum.
  • Treatment uses phenylbutazone and calcium borogluconate.
  • Both formalin-killed and attenuated vaccines exist.

posts.post_title: Vector family primarily responsible for BEF…
posts.post_content: Which insect family is primarily responsible for transmitting Bovine Ephemeral Fever virus?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Ceratopogonidae (sand flies)

The virus is transmitted mainly by sand flies of family Ceratopogonidae.

Correct Option Explanation

Mosquitoes such as Aedes, Anopheles and Culex, along with biting midges, also contribute to transmission.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Ixodidae hard ticks are not implicated as BEF vectors in the source.
  • Simuliidae (black flies) are not cited as vectors for BEF here.
  • Tabanidae horse flies are not the primary vector family described.
Know More
  • Strong wind can carry vectors over long distances.
  • Epizootics are associated with recent rainfall.
  • Disease is not reported in goat, sheep, pig or dog.
  • Incubation period ranges from 2–10 days.

posts.post_title: Fatal outcome proportion in overt Enzootic B…
posts.post_content: Approximately what percentage of cattle infected with Bovine Leukemia Virus go on to develop overt clinical lymphosarcoma?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: About 2%

Only around 2% of BLV-infected cattle develop clinical disease.

Correct Option Explanation

Those that do develop disease die after a long clinical course lasting weeks to months.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • About 20% overstates the true proportion that develops overt lymphosarcoma.
  • About 50% is far higher than the actual reported clinical disease rate.
  • About 80% actually corresponds to the proportion of a herd that may be inapparently infected, not diseased.
Know More
  • Most infections occur in dairy cattle over 2 years of age.
  • Maternal antibody protects calves for 5–6 months.
  • Commonly affected organs include lymph nodes, heart, abomasum.
  • Eradication relies on testing and removal of seropositive animals.

posts.post_title: Genus and family of Blue Tongue virus
posts.post_content: Blue Tongue virus (BTV) belongs to which genus and family?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Orbivirus, Reoviridae

BTV is a double-stranded RNA virus, genus Orbivirus, family Reoviridae.

Correct Option Explanation

It primarily affects sheep, causing catarrhal inflammation without vesicle formation, unlike FMD.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Pestivirus/Flaviviridae describes BVDV, not BTV.
  • Aphthovirus/Picornaviridae describes FMD virus, not BTV.
  • Rhabdovirus/Rhabdoviridae describes the Bovine Ephemeral Fever virus, not BTV.
Know More
  • Disease was first reported in India in 1964.
  • Spread mainly by Culicoides midges.
  • Young sheep under 1 year are more prone.
  • Horses, dogs, cats are not naturally susceptible.

posts.post_title: Vector genus responsible for Blue Tongue tra…
posts.post_content: Blue Tongue disease is primarily transmitted through blood-sucking midges of which genus?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Culicoides

Culicoides midges are the principal vectors of Blue Tongue virus.

Correct Option Explanation

Sheep keds (Melophagus ovinus) and mosquitoes may also mechanically transmit the disease.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Anopheles mosquitoes are only minor mechanical vectors, not the principal one.
  • Ixodes ticks are not implicated in Blue Tongue transmission.
  • Glossina (tsetse flies) transmit trypanosomiasis, not Blue Tongue.
Know More
  • Cattle act as reservoir and amplifying hosts.
  • Incubation period is about one week.
  • Acute-form morbidity is around 50%.
  • Recovered sheep remain immune for about 6 months.

posts.post_title: Species most susceptible to clinical Blue To…
posts.post_content: Blue Tongue is basically a clinical disease of which species, while other ruminants act mostly as non-clinical carriers?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Sheep

Blue Tongue is basically a disease of sheep.

Correct Option Explanation

Goats, cattle and wild ruminants show only milder symptoms and can act as non-clinical carriers.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Cattle serve mainly as reservoir/amplifying hosts, not the primarily affected species.
  • Goats exhibit only mild symptoms, unlike the severe disease seen in sheep.
  • Buffalo is not identified as the primary clinically affected species.
Know More
  • Merino sheep are particularly susceptible to the abortive form.
  • Chronic cases show extensive necrosis of the dental pad.
  • Blood-stained diarrhoea, when it occurs, is always fatal.
  • Live vaccines are contraindicated in pregnant sheep.

posts.post_title: Age for first vaccination against Blue Tongu…
posts.post_content: At what age are lambs typically first vaccinated against Blue Tongue?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: 6 months

Lambs are vaccinated at 6 months of age with an annual booster.

Correct Option Explanation

Vaccination is done several weeks before service and before the onset of the rainy season, when vector activity rises.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • 1 month is too young for the described first Blue Tongue vaccination age.
  • 3 weeks is far earlier than the stated vaccination schedule for lambs.
  • 2 years is later than the actual first vaccination age described.
Know More
  • Live, attenuated, avianated vaccines are used.
  • Vaccines may be monovalent or quadrivalent.
  • Vector control uses insecticides and water management.
  • Differential diagnoses include FMD and malignant catarrhal fever.

posts.post_title: Egg age used for primary isolation of Blue T…
posts.post_content: Blue Tongue virus can most readily be isolated by inoculation into embryonated chicken eggs of what age?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: 10–12 days old

BTV is most readily isolated in 10–12-day-old embryonated chicken eggs.

Correct Option Explanation

Primary isolation is also possible using intracerebral inoculation of new-born mice or monolayer cultures like BHK-21.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • 1–3-day-old eggs are too immature for the stated isolation method.
  • 18–20-day-old eggs are near hatching age, not the stated window.
  • Freshly laid eggs are not embryonated enough for viral isolation.
Know More
  • Cytopathic effect appears within 24–72 hours in cell culture.
  • Other diagnostic tests include CFT, AGID and ELISA.
  • Predisposing factors include poor nutrition and worm burden.

  • Organisms appear as coccoid forms (0.5–1.0 µm) attached to erythrocyte surfaces on Giemsa staining.
  • Rod-shaped forms of 1–3 µm can occasionally be seen.
  • Chronic subclinical disease makes the organism difficult to detect in blood smears.
  • Control includes use of disposable needles and arthropod control on pets.

posts.post_title: Distinguishing feature of Eimeria oocyst str…
posts.post_content: The sporulated Eimeria oocyst, considered the infective stage, contains how many sporocysts and sporozoites?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: 4 sporocysts, each with 2 sporozoites

The sporulated oocyst contains 4 sporocysts, each with 2 sporozoites, totalling 8 sporozoites — the infective stage.

Correct Option Explanation

The oocyst also has a refractile outer shell, sometimes with a micropyle covered by a polar cap.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • 2 sporocysts with 4 sporozoites each is a reversed, incorrect structural description.
  • 1 sporocyst with 8 sporozoites does not match the actual 4-sporocyst structure described.
  • 8 sporocysts with 1 sporozoite each is not the structure described for Eimeria oocysts.
Know More
  • Sporulation typically occurs outside the host.
  • Prepatent period in poultry coccidiosis is about 5 days.
  • Mature schizonts appear in a crescent shape, described as resembling a sliced onion.
  • Macrogametocytes have a large central nucleus with peripheral granules.

posts.post_title: Environmental condition lethal to Eimeria oo…
posts.post_content: Which of the following environmental conditions is described as lethal to both sporulated and unsporulated Eimeria oocysts?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Direct sunlight and temperatures above 56°C

Direct sunlight and temperatures above 56°C are lethal to Eimeria oocysts through desiccation.

Correct Option Explanation

Chemical disinfectants like 10% ammonia or methyl bromide are also effective at killing oocysts.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • 90% relative humidity is actually a favourable condition for oocyst survival and sporulation, not a lethal one.
  • 25–32°C is the optimum temperature range for sporulation, not a lethal condition.
  • Moderate shade with moist bedding provides favourable conditions for oocyst survival, not lethal desiccation.
Know More
  • Oocysts can survive in soil for about a year, especially during winter.
  • Freezing below 10°C under cool, dry conditions also kills oocysts.
  • Bacterial or fungal growth is lethal to the parasite.
  • Mechanical carriers include sparkling beetles and migratory birds.
